alignment_floor_note: Portuguese is the deck being shown, so it takes the strictest floor. Supply makes this nearly free: the harvest holds 44.6 candidates for the 10 a card displays, so a rejected candidate is replaced by the next subtitle row rather than by Tatoeba. Measured over the 10,000-card harvest, moving 0.30 -> 0.70 costs 76 of 99,719 displayed examples (0.08%), takes cards short of ten from 54 to 65, and moves the Tatoeba share only 27.6% -> 29.5% -- the subtitle register survives. The worst one percent of the deck improves from 0.502 to 0.708. Above 0.80 it starts to bite (118 short cards).
variety_note: European Portuguese against Brazilian. estar+gerund vs estar a+infinitive is the sharpest structural split; the rest is lexis and address. Measured on the Portuguese bank: 28.4% Brazilian-marked, 6.4% European-marked, 65.5% unmarked -- so an unmarked sentence is undetectable, not neutral.
